note: Counterexamples to the eval OUTCOME CONTRACT (ADOPT-M-05.01). Each fixture is INDEPENDENT of any external runner: it describes a defective run shape and the TYPED outcome (with its unit) a conforming runner must produce for it. THE PRESENCE OF A FIXTURE NEVER MEANS A SUCCESSFUL RUN — none of these cases claims an executed PASS; every expected outcome here is a refusal, a TIMEOUT or a NOT_RUN, recorded with the tool availability that produced it. Adapting an existing runner to consume these is FIX-EV-01's implementation, deliberately separate.

expected.why: a run past its budget is TIMEOUT — never scored on whatever partial output exists
a result missing a required metric is INVALID_RUN — an absent number is not a zero
a flat runs directory cannot attribute artifacts to runs — nothing in it is scoreable
two labels over one config digest mean the labels are decoration — a comparison of a thing with itself
a pass with empty evidence is an assertion, not a result
feedback newer than its last read has not entered the loop — the next iteration is NOT_RUN until it is read, never silently skipped
